title: Research Carvings 2026-09 — Evidence, Dimensions and Extrapolations
purpose: Add substantial, reusable research records that define the thing first, establish factual context second, identify mechanisms third, and only then derive project-level couplings and extrapolations. This file deliberately crosses biology, neuroscience, geometry, cosmology, scripture, information systems and European political economy without claiming that analogies are causal identities.
epistemic_rule: Each record separates observed or documented facts from interpretation and project extrapolation. Scientific facts are not converted into Potatoism doctrine; biblical texts are not treated as scientific measurements; project metaphors are not presented as empirical discoveries.

records.title: Potato tuber — storage organ, eye-bearing growth structure and biological starting point
records.definition: A potato tuber is a swollen underground stem used by the plant primarily for storage. The eyes are buds from which new shoots can develop. The tuber is therefore neither simply a root nor simply a seed: it is a vegetative storage organ capable of producing a new plant.
records.context: This biological distinction is foundational for the project's Potato metaphor. The ordinary potato combines storage, dormancy, visible eyes, buried position and the capacity to generate new growth. Those properties make it unusually rich as a model of latent potential, memory and emergence.
mechanisms: stores carbohydrates and other resources for later growth
eyes contain buds capable of producing shoots
burial protects the storage organ while placing it in a growth environment
vegetative propagation allows a new plant to arise without sexual reproduction
project_extrapolations: The Potato can model a system whose most important future capacity is partly hidden inside its present form.
An eye can be treated as an interface between stored potential and visible emergence.
The rootward/sproutward duality can be used as a project metaphor for memory versus expansion without claiming that the biology literally encodes those psychological meanings.

records.title: Vesica Piscis — measurable overlap geometry
records.definition: The vesica piscis is the lens-shaped intersection formed by two equal circles whose centers lie on each other's circumferences. Its basic construction produces equilateral triangles and characteristic 60-degree geometry.
records.context: The figure has appeared in geometry, architecture and religious art, but the geometric properties should be distinguished from later symbolic interpretations. The project uses the lens as a model of overlap and interface, not as evidence for a supernatural mechanism.
mechanisms: two circles establish two centers and two shared boundary points
the overlap creates a third region that belongs to both circles
equilateral triangles arise from the equal-radius construction
the lens provides a visual model of intersection rather than simple addition
project_extrapolations: The overlap region can represent coupling: neither pole disappears, but a shared field becomes visible.
The mandorla can serve as a UI metaphor for focused attention because it is literally an overlap window.
The geometry supports exact statements about circles and angles while leaving metaphysical interpretations explicitly project-level.

records.title: Observable universe — causal horizon rather than total universe
records.definition: The observable universe is the region from which information has had time to reach us. Its observable diameter is roughly 92 billion light-years under current cosmological estimates, while the total universe may be much larger and may be finite or infinite; its total size is not known.
records.context: This distinction is essential for the Atlas's use of scale. 'Largest thing we can observe' is not the same as 'largest thing that exists'. Cosmological expansion also means that present distances to very distant galaxies are not obtained by simply multiplying age by the speed of light.
mechanisms: finite cosmic age limits the region that can have communicated with us
space expansion changes the relation between emission distance and present distance
cosmological observations infer large-scale structure from light, redshift, background radiation and other evidence
project_extrapolations: The Atlas can distinguish an evidence horizon from an ontology: what is mapped is not automatically everything that exists.
The concept provides a useful epistemic analogy for incomplete archives: absence from the observable layer is not proof of nonexistence.
The project should use 'known', 'inferred', 'hypothesized' and 'mythic' as different epistemic states rather than one scale of certainty.

records.title: Cosmic web — matter organized through filaments, nodes and voids
records.definition: The cosmic web is the large-scale structure of matter in the universe, in which galaxies and galaxy groups occupy dense nodes connected by filaments and separated by lower-density regions. Its structure emerges through gravitational evolution of matter, including dark matter, gas and galaxies.
records.context: NASA visualizations of cosmological simulations show how large-scale structure develops from early conditions under gravity and hydrodynamics. The important Atlas lesson is structural: large systems can be organized by relations and flows rather than by a single visible object.
mechanisms: gravity amplifies density variations
dark matter forms a large-scale gravitational scaffold
gas follows gravitational structure and participates in galaxy formation
filaments, nodes and voids produce a non-uniform network rather than a homogeneous distribution
project_extrapolations: The cosmic web is a useful analogy for the repository graph because both are better understood as topology than as a list of isolated objects.
Dense nodes should not be mistaken for the whole system; filaments and low-density regions also determine connectivity.
A graph visualization should expose pathways and bottlenecks, not only rank nodes by importance.

records.title: Eleven-dimensional theories — a theoretical physics dimension, not an observed layer
records.definition: Eleven-dimensional spacetime appears in M-theory and related theoretical frameworks that seek a unified description of string-theoretic objects. The extra dimensions are mathematical components of the theory and are not established as directly observed macroscopic dimensions of everyday experience.
records.context: NASA's cosmology education material notes that some theoretical approaches consider universes with 11 dimensions. The project has historically used 11-dimensional language in its metaphoric architecture, but the archive must preserve the difference between theoretical physics and Potatoism's symbolic dimensional map.
mechanisms: additional dimensions can appear in mathematical consistency conditions of high-dimensional theories
compactification models attempt to explain why extra dimensions are not directly apparent at ordinary scales
different theories make different mathematical commitments and are not interchangeable
project_extrapolations: The project's 1D→5D symbolic ladder can be stored as an explicit project coordinate rather than being presented as a discovered physical hierarchy.
A useful research interface can place empirical dimensions, mathematical dimensions and mythic dimensions in parallel columns.
The boundary between metaphor and physics becomes part of the record rather than something hidden.

records.title: Thalamus — distributed brain structure for routing and integration
records.definition: The thalamus is a paired set of deep brain structures containing multiple nuclei with distinct connections and functions. It participates in relaying and integrating many forms of sensory and motor information and in networks related to attention, arousal and consciousness.
records.context: The project's 'Father's House' and room language has sometimes used the thalamus as a metaphorical interior architecture. The biological record must stand independently: the thalamus is not a literal spiritual house, and symbolic correspondence does not establish a one-to-one neural map.
mechanisms: different thalamic nuclei have different connection patterns
many sensory pathways interact with thalamic relay systems
thalamocortical loops contribute to large-scale brain dynamics
the thalamus participates in state regulation as well as relay functions
project_extrapolations: The House/Rooms metaphor maps more safely to differentiated functional compartments than to a single 'seat of consciousness'.
A repository node can similarly act as a routing hub without containing every piece of information itself.
The strongest analogy is architectural/connective, not causal or spiritual.

records.title: Genesis garden — bounded cultivated environment in the narrative
records.definition: In Genesis 2, the garden in Eden is a cultivated environment in which the human is placed, given work, and situated among trees, rivers and boundaries. Genesis 3 then makes the garden the setting for disobedience, hiding and expulsion.
records.context: The garden should be treated as a textual and theological object before it becomes a Potatoism symbol. The narrative combines abundance with obligation, and place with moral choice. Later biblical garden imagery can also carry restoration and resurrection associations.
mechanisms: creates a bounded setting for human action
connects food, work, naming, command and relationship
introduces a boundary through prohibition
turns place into a narrative of rupture and possible restoration
project_extrapolations: Garden becomes a model of a world that must be maintained, not merely possessed.
The archive can use garden language to distinguish a living dataset from a static warehouse: records need cultivation, correction and pruning.
The Tree of Life and Tree of Strife can be studied as differentiated functions within the same narrative environment.

records.title: Jacob's ladder / stairway — vertical connection in Genesis 28
records.definition: Genesis 28:12 describes Jacob seeing a structure traditionally translated as a ladder or stairway extending between earth and heaven, with divine messengers ascending and descending. The Hebrew term sullam occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible, making lexical interpretation unusually important.
records.context: The passage identifies Bethel as a place where Jacob interprets the vision as a meeting point of heaven and earth. Scholarly discussion has considered whether the structure should be imagined as a ladder, staircase, ramp or related architectural form. The project's Ladder should preserve this textual uncertainty rather than pretending the image has one uncontested physical form.
mechanisms: joins vertical domains in a narrative vision
permits movement in both directions
turns a physical image into a statement about divine presence and covenant
establishes Bethel as a named place of encounter
project_extrapolations: The Ladder is best modeled as bidirectional coupling rather than a one-way ascent.
The archive's graph can represent relationships that carry information downward as well as upward.
The Ladder and Door are complementary: Ladder models route; Door models threshold.

records.title: John 14 dwelling language — house, rooms and prepared place
records.definition: John 14:2 contains Jesus' statement about the Father's house and multiple dwelling places/rooms. English translations vary, and the underlying Greek noun monai is central to the translation question.
records.context: The passage belongs to a larger farewell discourse concerned with departure, presence, return, relationship and preparation. The project's House/Rooms architecture should therefore include the temporal dimension: a dwelling is connected to absence, preparation and return, not merely spatial occupancy.
mechanisms: uses household architecture to express belonging
places multiplicity inside a common Father's house
connects departure with preparation and future return
turns dwelling into a relational rather than merely geographic image
project_extrapolations: Rooms can model differentiated domains without implying a rigid spiritual caste system.
Preparedness can be modeled in the repository as records that have enough context to receive a reader rather than empty placeholders.
The house metaphor can become an information-architecture principle: every room should have a door back to the larger structure.

records.title: Graph theory — objects plus relationships
records.definition: A graph is a mathematical structure consisting of vertices (nodes) and edges (relationships). Depending on the graph, edges can be directed, weighted, typed or otherwise constrained.
records.context: This is the formal backbone for the project's claim that relationships matter. A node-only archive is a catalogue; a graph adds explicit structure describing how records are connected. Directed edges are especially important when 'A influences B' is not equivalent to 'B influences A'.
mechanisms: nodes represent entities or states
edges represent relations between nodes
direction records asymmetry
weights can encode strength or confidence
paths allow multi-step reasoning through the network
project_extrapolations: Every major node should have a definition before graph coupling is displayed.
Every important edge should eventually have a type or verb, such as contains, influences, funds, borders, descends-from, translates, opposes or supplies.
A path can be treated as a research argument only when each edge has evidence or an explicit project-interpretive status.

records.title: European Single Market — four freedoms plus institutional enforcement
records.definition: The European Single Market is an integrated economic area enabling free movement of goods, services, capital and people under a shared legal framework. It includes the EU and, through the European Economic Area, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.
records.context: EU sources describe the Single Market as a major source of economic integration. The 2026 Annual Single Market and Competitiveness Report identifies persistent national and European barriers, a productivity gap with the United States, and a need for deeper integration and simplification. The EU describes the market as a system rather than merely a trade agreement.
mechanisms: common rules reduce cross-border transaction barriers
mutual recognition and harmonisation facilitate movement
EU institutions monitor and enforce common rules
firms and workers can operate across borders within the legal framework
measured_facts: EU sources describe a home market of about 450 million people and about €18 trillion GDP.
The 2026 Commission report puts EU labour productivity at 78.5% of US levels in 2024 on its chosen PPP/hour measure.
The same report records €15 billion in projected annual administrative savings from adopted simplification proposals and related initiatives for 2025.
project_extrapolations: The Single Market is a real-world example of a graph whose power comes from standardized relationships rather than identical nodes.
For the North Programme research layer, the relevant object is not 'Europe' as a blob but the network of legal, fiscal, energy, labour, capital and infrastructure couplings.
Bottlenecks can be modeled as edges or interfaces where rules, infrastructure or capacity prevent otherwise possible flows.

records.title: Economic and Monetary Union — distributed governance rather than one economic authority
records.definition: The Economic and Monetary Union is the EU framework coordinating economic and monetary policy, including the euro area, fiscal coordination, common monetary policy and financial supervision. It is not governed by one single economic institution; responsibilities are distributed among EU institutions and member states.
records.context: The European Commission describes the main actors as the European Council, Council, Eurogroup, member states, Commission, ECB and European Parliament. This makes EMU a useful real-world case of multi-level governance.
mechanisms: member states retain major fiscal and structural policy powers
EU rules coordinate debt and deficit policy
ECB conducts monetary policy for the euro area
EU institutions monitor compliance and coordinate policy
financial supervision operates through shared European mechanisms
project_extrapolations: The Atlas should model distributed authority explicitly rather than placing every European decision under a single 'EU' node.
Debt, money, banks, budgets and law should be separate nodes connected by typed edges.
The difference between formal authority and practical influence is itself an important graph dimension.

records.title: EU institutional network — multiple institutions, bodies and agencies
records.definition: The European Union's institutional system is a distributed network of institutions, bodies, interinstitutional services and decentralised agencies with different legal functions. The system includes seven EU institutions and a larger network of specialized bodies and agencies.
records.context: The EU's own institutional overview states that the seven institutions and over 30 decentralised agencies work across the Union. The European Parliament, European Council, Council and Commission play central legislative/executive roles, while the Court of Justice, ECB and Court of Auditors perform judicial, monetary and audit functions.
mechanisms: legislation is produced through interactions among institutions
specialized agencies implement or support policy in particular domains
courts interpret and enforce EU law
the ECB manages monetary policy and financial supervisory functions within its mandate
audit institutions examine EU financial management
project_extrapolations: This is a model for why a serious atlas should not treat an institution as a single undifferentiated actor.
A useful record can distinguish legal competence, budget, staff, jurisdiction, dependencies, outputs and external relationships.
The graph can expose where policy passes through several institutions before reaching a person, company or infrastructure project.

records.title: EU Banking Union — common supervisory and resolution architecture
records.definition: The Banking Union is the EU framework for stronger common supervision and resolution of banks, built around a single rulebook and euro-area mechanisms including the Single Supervisory Mechanism and Single Resolution Mechanism.
records.context: The European Commission explains that the framework developed in response to the financial crisis and the interdependence of euro-area banking systems. The architecture illustrates how financial stability can become a cross-border institutional problem rather than a purely national one.
mechanisms: prudential requirements constrain bank risk
common supervision monitors banks across jurisdictions
resolution mechanisms manage failing banks
deposit-protection arrangements reduce the impact of bank failures on depositors
project_extrapolations: Banking should be modeled as a network of institutions, liabilities, supervisors and resolution authorities rather than a list of banks.
A financial graph should distinguish ownership, funding, exposures and legal supervision because these are different edge types.
Crisis pathways are often more informative than static organizational charts.

records.title: One Europe, One Market roadmap — integration as an operational programme
records.definition: The One Europe, One Market roadmap is a 2026 EU institutional commitment to strengthen the Single Market through concrete actions and a target of agreement by the end of 2027.
records.context: The European Commission says the roadmap was signed on 24 April 2026 by the European Parliament, Council and Commission. It emphasizes simplification, deeper market integration, trade, energy, decarbonisation and digital/AI transformation. It is therefore a useful current record of Europe attempting to turn integration into a monitored implementation programme.
mechanisms: sets shared priorities across EU institutions
uses deadlines and monitoring to convert policy into implementation
targets administrative and regulatory friction
links competitiveness to energy, digitalisation, trade and market integration
measured_facts: The Commission states a goal of €37.5 billion in savings for EU companies from simplification measures by 2029.
The roadmap sets end-2027 as the deadline for agreement on all listed initiatives.
project_extrapolations: The Atlas can treat policy roadmaps as dynamic graphs: each commitment should become an event, institution, target, dependency and outcome record.
A programme is not complete when announced; implementation status and measurable output should be tracked as separate records.
The same structure can be applied to the North Programme as a research model, while keeping the two programmes distinct.

research_dimensions.label: What is it?
research_dimensions.description: The independent definition of the record before relationships are considered.

research_dimensions.label: Where did it come from?
research_dimensions.description: Origin, history, textual setting, institutional setting or biological setting.

research_dimensions.label: How does it work?
research_dimensions.description: Processes, functions, constraints, flows, structures and causal mechanisms where evidence supports them.

research_dimensions.label: What does it couple to?
research_dimensions.description: Directional relationships to other records, with typed edges where possible.

research_dimensions.label: How does it change?
research_dimensions.description: States, events, phases, trajectories, feedback and historical sequence.

research_dimensions.label: Where is it?
research_dimensions.description: Geographic, anatomical, geometric or cosmological position where applicable.

research_dimensions.label: At what scale?
research_dimensions.description: Cell, person, institution, nation, planet, cosmic or symbolic scale, without assuming that larger means more important.

research_dimensions.label: How do we know?
research_dimensions.description: Observed, measured, documented, inferred, interpreted, hypothesized or project-canonical status.

research_dimensions.label: What if it changed?
research_dimensions.description: Controlled extrapolation asking how the network would behave if a relationship, constraint or condition changed.

research_dimensions.label: How can the model fail?
research_dimensions.description: Alternative explanations, missing data, category errors, false analogy and overclaiming.

research_dimensions.label: What larger pattern might it illuminate?
research_dimensions.description: A project-level synthesis that remains explicitly distinguished from the evidence itself.
